slides.headline: New Zealand voted. Nobody won.
slides.subline: **Final results are in.** Here is what a hung parliament means.

slides.body: Final New Zealand election results, confirmed on **Nov 27**, show neither the governing right bloc nor the left bloc has a [[majority]].
New Zealand votes for **parties**, not just local winners. A party needs **5% of the vote** to enter parliament. A newcomer cleared it and is now the [[decider]].
AP says the centrist **Opportunity Party** now holds the balance. Whichever bloc it backs can form the [[next government]].
Weeks of **coalition talks**. If no bloc can build a majority, New Zealand could even face [[a fresh election]].
Should a small party hold this much power? Tell us below.
